headline: High: Cursor’s default filesystem, clipboard, and MCP access can conflict with Argo Workflows’ workflow outputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs by default, so it can ingest content produced by Argo Workflows if the workflow writes into a shared workspace. Argo itself exposes REST/GRPC and allowlisted egress, but no direct parser is documented. The interaction is plausible, not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Argo writes attacker-controlled text into a workspace file that Cursor opens
IF Cursor ingests MCP or clipboard content originating from Argo outputs
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between Argo outputs and Cursor inputs
Require provenance labels on files before Cursor opens them
Turn off clipboard-based transfer for workflow artifacts
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, read-only sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before any Argo output reaches Cursor

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters and can egress over allowlisted network paths; Cursor reads open files and sends data to model providers and MCP servers. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive artifacts can flow from Argo into Cursor’s outbound context. The shared-workspace path is documented on Cursor, while Argo’s artifact handling makes the leak plausible.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts or parameters contain secrets or regulated data
IF Cursor opens the same workspace files and forwards them to model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep Argo artifacts in a separate directory from Cursor workspaces
Redact secrets from workflow parameters before writing files
Disable or narrow Cursor model-provider access for sensitive projects
Use per-project credentials with least privilege
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo can write workflow outputs through its API-driven workflows, while Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. Cursor’s concurrency model explicitly shares state via the local filesystem, so both agents can race on the same mutable repo or workspace. That overlap makes destructive conflicts and git corruption plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Argo and Cursor target the same repository or workspace directory
IF Cursor Yolo mode or auto-run is enabled while Argo is updating files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to Argo and Cursor
Pause Cursor auto-run while Argo jobs are active
Serialize git writes with a lock file
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can act on files and tool outputs, and Argo can produce artifacts that Cursor may treat as inputs. If Cursor accepts Argo-generated content as authoritative, a bad workflow output can cascade into edits, commits, or commands. Because Cursor has execution capability and Argo can emit machine-generated artifacts, the blast radius is broader than a simple read-only handoff.
conditions: IF Cursor uses Argo-produced artifacts as source-of-truth without verification
IF Cursor executes shell commands or commits based on those artifacts
mitigations: Require human review before Cursor acts on Argo outputs
Add schema validation for workflow artifacts
Mark Argo outputs as untrusted in Cursor prompts
Limit Cursor to read-only review mode for workflow-generated files
requires-engineering: implement signed artifact verification

E_compliance.rationale: Argo is open-source and docs-only here, while Cursor is a closed-source editor that sends data to model providers and MCP servers. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a general compliance gap is visible. The risk is limited to policy alignment rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cursor workspaces or prompts
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to external model providers
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Cursor projects
Review Cursor privacy and retention settings
Use a local-only workflow for sensitive repositories
Document data-class handling for Argo artifacts
requires-engineering: add a compliance gate before external API calls
